title: NPCs that never repeat a line of dialogue: an AI researcher on where game dev is actually heading
author: DeskStrong3493
selftext:
Stumbled on this podcast episode with Shesh Narayan Gupta (AI researcher, data scientist, wrote a book on generative AI for game dev). Really good conversation, so I pulled the best bits with timestamps:

* NPCs as tiny LLMs ([17:47](https://l.meta.ai/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fyoutu.be%2FLjf0DUgBZSA%3Ft%3D1067&h=AUBME34tynYkVlMgfGp4qGo5efdxPDg-b_QwNEkU0N-x7Rz9YdyDLEIEIvZubWQJWbNQB93oU-jSVZwANIDWta6qzJCU9i_2ZLRhCxaFPBg0KAgd3KkmqA)) — instead of picking lines from a script, the characters just respond. Like a chatbot wearing a 3D model. Kind of wild to think about what that does to quest design.
* The fairness thing nobody talks about ([07:40](https://l.meta.ai/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fyoutu.be%2FLjf0DUgBZSA%3Ft%3D460&h=AUBME34tynYkVlMgfGp4qGo5efdxPDg-b_QwNEkU0N-x7Rz9YdyDLEIEIvZubWQJWbNQB93oU-jSVZwANIDWta6qzJCU9i_2ZLRhCxaFPBg0KAgd3KkmqA)) — he gives this example where an NPC gatekeeper lets one player into a campaign and blocks another, just because the model guessed different genders. That's when the whole guardrail debate clicked for me.
* Some things have to stay hardcoded ([20:04](https://l.meta.ai/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fyoutu.be%2FLjf0DUgBZSA%3Ft%3D1204&h=AUBME34tynYkVlMgfGp4qGo5efdxPDg-b_QwNEkU0N-x7Rz9YdyDLEIEIvZubWQJWbNQB93oU-jSVZwANIDWta6qzJCU9i_2ZLRhCxaFPBg0KAgd3KkmqA)) — his example is a shopkeeper. If everything runs on AI, you could sweet-talk your way into a gun that's supposed to be locked behind missions. That breaks the game.
* Guardrails vs lag ([37:14](https://l.meta.ai/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fyoutu.be%2FLjf0DUgBZSA%3Ft%3D2234&h=AUBME34tynYkVlMgfGp4qGo5efdxPDg-b_QwNEkU0N-x7Rz9YdyDLEIEIvZubWQJWbNQB93oU-jSVZwANIDWta6qzJCU9i_2ZLRhCxaFPBg0KAgd3KkmqA)) — a safety check that makes an NPC take 15 seconds to reply is a non-starter. He walks through the tradeoff between fairness and response time from his own research.
* Games as the lab for AI safety ([48:54](https://l.meta.ai/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fyoutu.be%2FLjf0DUgBZSA%3Ft%3D2934&h=AUBME34tynYkVlMgfGp4qGo5efdxPDg-b_QwNEkU0N-x7Rz9YdyDLEIEIvZubWQJWbNQB93oU-jSVZwANIDWta6qzJCU9i_2ZLRhCxaFPBg0KAgd3KkmqA)) — his bigger point. Games let you build test scenarios and check guardrails fast, which is way harder to do with real world systems.

Anyway, full episode here: [https://youtu.be/Ljf0DUgBZSA](https://l.meta.ai/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fyoutu.be%2FLjf0DUgBZSA&h=AUBME34tynYkVlMgfGp4qGo5efdxPDg-b_QwNEkU0N-x7Rz9YdyDLEIEIvZubWQJWbNQB93oU-jSVZwANIDWta6qzJCU9i_2ZLRhCxaFPBg0KAgd3KkmqA)
